correctness.rationale: The exact C''' four-term objective is a positive linear combination of squares of norms of linear transforms in (x,y), hence jointly convex on product of the two closed polyhedral unit balls. Its global maximum can be realized at one of 36 ordered vertex pairs, which all lie on the sphere; the upper bound extends to sphere. Explicit 60-degree rotation, reflection and y-sign invariance split pairs into 12 equal/opposite and 24 distinct orbit pairs. Parallel pairs evaluate 1. Taking x=(1,1), y=(1,0), and 0<=m<=1/2 yields N(mx+(1−m)y)=1, N(mx−(1−m)y)=1−m, N(x−y)=1, N(x+y)=2, so F=1+3m/2−2m², always >=1 on interval. Polynomial derivative 3/2−4m gives unique maximum m=3/8 => 41/32, exactly lambda=3/8,5/8. Independently evaluated 36 pairs at exact rational checkpoints, including both symmetric maximizers, and checked analytic active branches. No statement about other normed planes or complex scalars.
risks: The exact profile relies on the four-term definition (including the exterior factor 1/2) in the cited primary paper; using the ordinary two-term constant would be a different theorem.
